Part 2&3 物品 OBJECTS

Describe a program or app on your computer or phone

描述你电脑或手机上的一个程序或APP

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a program or app on your computer or phone

  • What it is (它是什么)
  • How often you use it (你多久用一次)
  • When/how you use it (你什么时候/怎么用)
  • When/how you found it (你什么时候/怎么发现它的)
  • And explain how you feel about it (并谈谈你对它的感受)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a program or app on your computer or phone

I'd like to talk about WeChat, which is the app I use most often on my phone. It's basically a messaging app, but in my country it's become much more than that. First of all, what it is: WeChat is a social and messaging app developed in China. You can send text messages, voice messages and photos, make video calls, and share moments with your friends, which is like a personal feed. It's also used for payments, so many people use it to pay for things in shops and restaurants. As for how often I use it, honestly, I use it every day, probably dozens of times. It's the first app I open in the morning and the last one I check before I go to sleep. I mainly use it to chat with my friends and family, especially my girlfriend, and to keep up with group chats for my classes and hobbies. I found it a long time ago, back in middle school, when everyone around me started using it. At first I only used it to message friends, but over the years it's become a part of daily life, since almost everything, from paying bills to booking things, can be done through it. The reason I feel so strongly about it is that it keeps me connected to the people I care about. Even though I don't see my friends every day, we can still share what's happening in our lives through WeChat. Looking back, I think it's not just an app for me, it's how I stay close to the people around me.

讲的是微信，我手机上用得最多的应用。它本质是聊天软件，但在国内已经远不止如此。功能：发文字、语音、照片，视频通话，发朋友圈（像个人动态），还能支付，很多人用它付款。使用频率：每天用，一天几十次，早上第一个打开、睡前最后一个看；主要和亲友聊天，尤其是女朋友，还有班级和兴趣群聊。怎么发现的：初中时周围人都在用，一开始只用来发消息，后来成了生活的一部分，缴费、订东西都能用它。感受：它让我和在乎的人保持联系，即使不每天见面也能分享生活。对我来说它不只是应用，而是和身边人保持亲近的方式。

Q2What are the differences between old and young people when using apps?

I think the main difference is how easily they adapt. Young people pick up new apps quickly and use them for many purposes, like entertainment, shopping and socialising. Older people, on the other hand, tend to use only a few apps and prefer simple ones, like messaging or news apps. They also need more time to learn new features and sometimes ask younger family members for help. So I'd say young people are more flexible, while older people value simplicity.

主要区别是适应能力。年轻人学新应用很快，用途也多：娱乐、购物、社交；老年人往往只用少数几个应用，偏好简单的，如聊天或新闻应用，学新功能需要更多时间，有时还向年轻家人求助。年轻人更灵活，老年人更看重简单。

Q3Why do some people not like using apps?

There are a few reasons. Some people find apps complicated and confusing, especially older users who didn't grow up with smartphones. Others worry about privacy, since many apps collect personal data, and some people are concerned about spending too much time on their phones. On top of that, some people simply prefer face-to-face communication and feel that apps make relationships less personal. So I think it's a mix of practical difficulty and personal preference.

原因有几个。有些人觉得应用复杂难懂，尤其是没在智能手机时代长大的老年用户；有人担心隐私，因为很多应用收集个人数据，还有人担心在手机上花太多时间；此外有些人就是更喜欢面对面交流，觉得应用让关系变得不那么个人化。这是实际困难和个人偏好的混合。

Q4What apps are popular in your country? Why?

In my country, WeChat is probably the most popular app, because it combines messaging, payments and social media in one place, which means people use it for almost everything. Short video apps like Douyin are also extremely popular, since they're entertaining and easy to use. Shopping apps like Taobao are widely used too, because they make buying things convenient. I think these apps succeed because they're simple, useful and deeply connected to daily life.

国内最流行的应用大概是微信，因为它把聊天、支付和社交媒体合在一起，人们几乎用它做所有事；抖音这类短视频应用也非常流行，有趣又易用；淘宝等购物应用也广泛使用，因为买东西方便。这些应用成功是因为简单、实用、和日常生活紧密相连。

Q5Should parents limit their children's use of computer programs and computer games? Why and how?

Yes, I think parents should set some limits, because too much screen time can affect children's health, eyesight and schoolwork. That said, completely banning games isn't a good idea either, since games can be a way to relax and even learn. A better approach is to set reasonable time limits, like one or two hours a day, and to encourage children to balance gaming with outdoor activities and homework. I think the key is guidance rather than strict control.

是的，父母应该设一些限制，因为屏幕时间过长会影响孩子的健康、视力和学业。不过完全禁止游戏也不好，游戏可以是放松甚至学习的方式。更好的做法是设合理的时间限制，比如每天一两小时，并鼓励孩子平衡游戏、户外活动和作业。关键是引导而不是严格控制。

Q6Do you think young people are more and more reliant on these programs?

Yes, I think young people are becoming increasingly reliant on apps, and it's hard to imagine life without them. We use apps for communication, study, work, shopping and entertainment, so almost every part of daily life depends on them. This has made things more convenient, but it also means young people may struggle when they can't use their phones, and some find it hard to focus without checking apps constantly. So I'd say the reliance is real, and it has both positive and negative sides.

是的，年轻人越来越依赖应用，很难想象没有它们的生活。我们用应用沟通、学习、工作、购物、娱乐，日常生活几乎每个部分都依赖它们。这让事情更方便，但也意味着不能用手机时年轻人会难受，有些人总忍不住刷应用、难以专注。依赖是真实的，有好有坏。

Q7What do you think about some countries banning children from using social media?

I think the intention behind such bans is understandable, since social media can expose children to harmful content and affect their mental health. However, I'm not sure a complete ban is the best solution, because social media also helps children stay connected with friends and learn new things. A more practical approach might be age limits and parental supervision, so children can use these platforms safely. On balance, I'd say the goal is right, but the method needs to be more flexible.

这类禁令的初衷可以理解，社交媒体可能让孩子接触有害内容、影响心理健康。但我不确定完全禁止是最好的办法，因为社交媒体也帮孩子和朋友保持联系、学习新东西。更实际的做法可能是年龄限制和家长监督，让孩子安全使用。总体目标是对的，但方式需要更灵活。
